title: Hardship Settlement Electronic Acceptance: The Signing Window to the First Payment
content:
# Hardship Settlement — Signing Window

When a consumer accepts a Hardship Settlement offer of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements by electronic signature, the Hardship Settlement signing window is the number of calendar days from the acceptance date to the due date of the first settlement payment.

**§1** The offered Hardship Settlement window is the number of calendar days from the offer date of that open offer to the first payment due date written on it, never more than 30 days.

**§2** The Hardship Settlement signing window is the offered Hardship Settlement window, never less than one day.

**§3** On electronic acceptance the first settlement payment falls due that many calendar days after the acceptance date, each later payment falls due the offer's payment interval after the one before it, and the offer's settlement amount is booked to the settlement once, on the acceptance date.

**§4** The signing window is formed in one pass: the offered window capped at 30 days, less any shortenings that apply taken together and subtracted once, plus any days added back, the result being never less than one day nor more than the capped offered window.

## Hypothetical worked example

An open Hardship Settlement offer dated day X shows its first payment due on day X plus 30, with three payments 30 days apart. The offered window is 30 days, which is at the 30-day cap, so the signing window is 30 days. If the consumer signs on day Y, the payments fall due on day Y plus 30, Y plus 60 and Y plus 90, and the settlement amount is booked once on day Y.

## Points of judgement

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Can the signing window be zero days? | No; it is never less than one day. |
| Can it be longer than the capped offered window? | No. |
| From which date are the days counted? | The acceptance date. |
| When is the settlement amount booked? | Once, on the acceptance date. |
